# C1 self-test fixture (review finding): a deliberately vulnerable pin, so
# the "pip-audit (ignore-list) — blocking" step has something real to block
# on. .pip-audit-ignore alongside this file does NOT list any of the IDs
# this pin actually triggers, so that step must fail with
# "pip-audit reported findings not present in .pip-audit-ignore".
#
# ROUND-4 FIX (HIGH, caught by a real CI job log - run 31632092745, job
# 94233134598): this fixture used to pin `PyYAML==5.3`, and it had never
# once reached the intended FINDING branch. `bandit==1.9.4` (installed
# unconditionally by the reusable workflow's own "pip install tools" step)
# requires `PyYAML>=5.3.1`, so the frozen environment pip-audit re-resolves
# (`pip freeze --all --exclude-editable` -> `pip-audit -r <snapshot>`)
# contained `bandit==1.9.4` AND `PyYAML==5.3` together - an impossible
# resolve. pip-audit died with "internal pip failure: ... conflicting
# dependencies" BEFORE ever looking up PyYAML's CVEs, hitting the step's
# CRASH branch ("::error::pip-audit failed to run") instead. The job still
# went red, and the paired assert job only checked the job-level result, so
# the entire "genuine pip-audit finding correctly blocked" path was never
# exercised by real CI even once.
#
# Fixed by pinning a vulnerable package that NOTHING in the tool set depends
# on. Jinja2 is not a dependency (direct or transitive) of ruff, pytest,
# mypy, bandit, or pip-audit - verified against a clean venv containing
# exactly the workflow's five pinned tools - so there is no shared
# requirement for a tool's own version floor to ever conflict with. Picking
# a PyYAML patch above bandit's floor would have fixed today's symptom while
# leaving the same failure class one bandit bump away; this removes the
# class.
#
# Verified locally against the real PyPI advisory data with the pinned
# pip-audit==2.10.1, both directions:
#   - unignored: exit 1, "Found 3 known vulnerabilities in 1 package"
#     (PYSEC-2026-1471 / PYSEC-2026-1475 / PYSEC-2026-1472, fixed in
#     jinja2 3.1.5/3.1.6) - the FINDING branch, which is what this fixture
#     exists to prove blocks.
#   - all three ignored via --ignore-vuln: exit 0, "No known vulnerabilities
#     found, 3 ignored" - proving the ignore-list mechanism itself works, so
#     the blocking result below is genuinely "not covered by the ignore
#     list", not "the ignore list does nothing".
# The paired assert job now greps this fixture job's real log for the
# rendered "##[error]pip-audit reported findings not present in
# .pip-audit-ignore" annotation AND for the ABSENCE of the crash annotation,
# so a repeat of the resolver-crash regression above can never again be
# silently satisfied by a job-level red.
#
# No .py files in this fixture, deliberately: pip-audit audits the
# environment snapshot (pip freeze --all --exclude-editable), not source
# code, so this needs to be the ONLY plausible failure point — a stray .py
# file would risk an unrelated ruff/bandit/mypy finding muddying which
# check actually blocked the gate (same discipline as node-lint-violation
# and python-test-failure).
Jinja2==3.1.4
